newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds firm on continued U.S. strength.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds firm on continued U.S. strength.

text.p: *Australian bonds started the week firm, largely in response to further strength in U.S. Treasuries on Friday following a balanced budget accord in Washington.
*April ANZ job ads due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bonds started the week firm, largely in response to further strength in U.S. Treasuries on Friday following a balanced budget accord in Washington.

The agreement between the Clinton administration and Rebulican leaders overshadowed a mixed response to the key U.S. labour force report, which while showed a smaller than expected rise in non-farm payrolls, it also saw unemployment fall to its lowest level in 23 years at 4.9 percent.
"We're largely reacting to the U.S., but we have taken it a bit further since the opening because we have lagged the U.S. in the few days," one trader at a European Bank said.

The local market has been under pressure in the past few sessions following a stronger than expected first quarter average weekly earnings report which killed off chances, albeit slim, of a further easing in monetary policy.

Treasurer Peter Costello said at the weekend that the annual wages growth rate at 4.6 percent was "a little high" for the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) and the government, but added that inflation was no longer a barrier to cut interest rates.
The RBA holds its month board meeting on Tuesday, but a majority of economists do not expect a change in policy to follow it with official interest rates staying at 6.0 percent.
However, further policy sensitive data is due for release this week with Australia's labour force report due on Thursday.
Economists expect there was a rebound in employment during April, but for the unemployment rate to remain stubbornly high at 8.7 percent.
On the same day, RBA governor Ian Macfarlane appears before a parliamentary financial committee.
The April ANZ job advertisement series is due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) may give some indication to this week's employment report.

The local market outperformed against the dollar bloc, apart from the short end of the Canadian yield curve. The Canadian out-paced the U.S. on Friday amid further strength in the Canadian dollar on waning fears of a U.S. policy tightening. Local bonds were little changed against New Zealand.
